children: A joint venture between two of Italy's biggest defense players signed an agreement with a total value of around 3.7 billion euros ($4.21 billion) to supply two destroyers to the Italian navy.

Shipbuilder Fincantieri and defense group Leonardo said Thursday that their joint venture Orizzonte Sistemi Navali secured the agreement with Occar, which organizes procurement for a group of European militaries. The contract is to develop and manufacture two new-generation DDX destroyers for the Italian naval force, and is worth around 1.8 billion euros for Fincantieri and 1.7 billion euros for Leonardo, of which a total of approximately 1.3 billion euros is in options, the two companies said.
Fincantieri will design and develop the naval platform and act as system integrator, while Leonardo will produce the ships' combat system. Delivery of the two destroyers is expected in 2033 and 2035.
The latest DDX model of destroyer features high levels of digitalization and automation, the two companies said.

"We are further strengthening our leadership in the naval defense sector and investing in the development of expertise, technologies and the supply chain, helping to consolidate Italy's industrial and technological sovereignty and the country's competitiveness in the European naval defense sector," Fincantieri Chief Executive Pierroberto Folgiero said.
